source.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Trajectory Data Curation for LoRA Fine-Tuning of Code Agents

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether held-out fine-tuning loss tracks first-action generation quality, using a proxy-evaluation method rather than the original pretraining scaling-law sweeps.
record.gate_note: The study reports a fine-tuning trajectory-count sweep and a cross-check between held-out CE loss and first-action generation. The trajectory-count loss results do not fit or test a power-law form, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper cites scaling-laws literature as rationale for CE loss as a proxy; it does not report results from those cited studies as its own.
record.test_reason: The study uses held-out CE loss as its evaluation proxy and cites Kaplan et al. as the rationale. Its only check on that choice compares LoRA fine-tuning loss with first-action ROUGE-L across four checkpoints of one 7B model. That is a validation of the study's own metric. It does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or model scale (V6). The 500/1,000/2,000-trajectory SFT sweep has three points and no power-law fit, so it cannot bear on V1, V2 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but incomplete. The central conclusion is that data quantity dominates quality filtering at 500–1,000 trajectories: about 12.7% loss reduction per doubling, against a quality gap under 1% that is not significant. The TopQ–Random gap widens to 3.6% at 2,000 (p=0.016), which the authors call a signal, not a confirmed crossover. Error-retry (B2) is the dominant quality sub-metric. The authors also say the first-action check validates CE loss as a proxy, while calling the n=4 evidence supporting rather than conclusive.
record.recipe_differences: This is LoRA SFT on agent trajectories with a 500–2,000 trajectory sweep and first-action proxy validation, not a pretraining parameter/token/compute scaling-law fit.
record.method_sensitivity: The first-action proxy uses four checkpoints and a 300-token generation budget; the paper notes that this budget affects action-type measurement. Loss and quality-filtering effects differ by training-set size and selection strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out Gold-set CE loss of LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-7B falls as SFT trajectories grow from 500 to 1,000 to 2,000. The per-doubling gains shrink (Random 12.6% then 6.5%; TopQ 12.7% then 9.1%), and no power law is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over 500–2,000 SFT agent trajectories, held-out trajectory loss falls with diminishing returns per doubling of data.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four checkpoints, SFT held-out CE loss is perfectly rank-correlated with first-action ROUGE-L (ρ = −1.00, n=4). File-Match accuracy does not track loss among the fine-tuned checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out SFT loss on agent trajectories orders first-action generation similarity but not file-targeting accuracy.

record.problems: The study tests one base model and one trajectory source. The CE-loss/ROUGE-L association uses only four checkpoints, with a minimum achievable two-sided p ≈ 0.083. The held-out test sets contain 200 trajectories each, and the trajectory-count sweep has only three scale points. The authors also report limitations from the 300-token generation budget.

untested.parts: Not tested: no pretraining runs and no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested: no fitted law is used to extrapolate.
Not tested. The SFT loss sweep has only three data sizes (500/1,000/2,000) within one 4x range, and no power law is fitted.
Not tested. Downstream performance is not related to pretraining loss or model scale. The SFT-loss vs first-action ROUGE-L check uses four checkpoints of one model.
Not tested: no exponents and no fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. [18] are cited only as justification for using CE loss as a capability proxy. The study is about SFT data curation for code agents. Table 2 rows not captured (untrained CE 0.9100, BottomQ-500, B2Only-500, Random/Low-Q test sets) and the Table 4 ablations do not bear on any version, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, training tokens, or compute over several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation is tested.
No architecture-depth or width comparison is made.
The study evaluates trajectory-count changes during SFT but does not test whether a power-law form holds in fine-tuning, repeated-data training, or other regimes.
Tests only a first-action generation proxy on four checkpoints; it does not test broad downstream-task performance, or predict performance from pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Four checkpoints (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Rank correlation of held-out CE loss with first-action ROUGE-L

conditions.value: 100 held-out Gold instances per checkpoint; up to 300 generated tokens

rows.measure: Spearman correlation between Gold-set CE loss and first-action ROUGE-L
rows.value: ρ = −1.00; n = 4; minimum achievable two-sided p ≈ 0.083
rows.uncertainty: Minimum achievable two-sided p ≈ 0.083; no claim of p < 0.001
rows.note: The authors describe the ordering as perfectly rank-correlated but caution that the four-checkpoint sample makes the evidence supporting rather than conclusive.
rows.check: Correlation of SFT held-out loss with first-action ROUGE-L, used to validate the study's own proxy. It involves neither pretraining loss nor model scale, and n=4 (minimum two-sided p ≈ 0.083).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: CE loss and first-action ROUGE-L have Spearman ρ = −1.00 across the four checkpoints, and ROUGE-L rises from 0.137 at baseline to 0.248 at Random-1000 (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: First-action file targeting in the four-checkpoint validation
reader_labels.reason: File-Match accuracy does not strictly track CE loss: it falls from 0.680 at Random-500 to 0.650 at Random-1000 and varies across the fine-tuned checkpoints (r6–r9).
